citations.claim: total energy jumps ~2960 J above initial at first violating step 12
energy conserved just before impact at step 11
heavy body leaves collision much faster than it entered

counterfactual.change: set restitution e of both bodies to 0 (was 0.6 and 1.0); removes elastic energy injection at impact, same 12 steps, no violation

explanation: No controller work and flat pre-impact energy rule out external forcing. The jump occurs exactly when the two fast bodies touch at step 12 (gap ~0.007, 24 substeps). Light body at ~53 m/s meets heavy body at ~54 m/s obliquely; after the impulse the heavy body exits at ~59 m/s and total energy rises ~12% with no work input. Likely cause: body-body impulse uses a stale/combined normal over substeps and/or positional correction pushes bodies apart along the line of centers adding potential-to-kinetic energy, injecting net energy for high-speed oblique impacts with restitution.
vision_note: The smaller upper circle moves down toward the larger lower circle across steps 9 to 11 until they make contact. At step 12 the small circle touches the upper-right side of the large circle with slight overlap, indicating a sudden oblique collision.
